ELV.thesis_one_line: A large US health insurer whose profits fell on rising medical costs; the price assumes no recovery, though management targets 12% growth in 2027.
kill_criteria: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance cut below $26.00 (now "at least $27.00", acc. 0001156039-26-000063), or Q3/Q4 adjusted EPS below $3.00 in either quarter (Q4'25 was $3.33).
Consolidated benefit expense ratio above 91.0% for FY26 (guidance "90.2% plus or minus 50 basis points", acc. 0001156039-26-000063; Q2'26 89.7%).
Prior-year reserve redundancies in H1'27 below $700m (H1'26 $1,195m; release table "Prior years redundancies").
Debt-to-capital (credit-agreement definition, consolidated, 10-Q MD&A) above 45% (now 40.8%; covenant 60%).
Any DOJ settlement, judgment or new accrual above $1.0bn in the Medicare risk-adjustment litigation.
key_adverse_facts: Adjusted EPS fell from ~$33.0 (2024) to $30.29 (2025) and is guided at least $27.00 for 2026; 2025 guidance was cut ~13% mid-year (from $34.15-$34.85 to ~$30.00)
H1'26 adjusted EPS of $20.03 includes ~$1.80 of non-recurring or below-the-line benefit; implied H2 only ~$7.00
Medicare Advantage membership -15.9% and Medicaid -4.3% y/y; benefit ratio up 80 bps in Q2'26 on government-business cost trend
DOJ False Claims Act suit on Medicare risk adjustment (filed March 2020) in discovery through 10 May 2027, unquantified; CMS notice accrual $935m (closed 13 Jul 2026, no sanctions)
Prior-year reserve redundancies shrinking (FY25 $1,290m = 1.0% of prior-year incurred vs $1,731m = 1.4% in FY24)
data_conflicts: Yahoo totalCash $37.5bn is consolidated cash plus investments, not parent liquidity (parent cash and investments ~$2.1bn)
b1 TTM FCF yield 7.3% vs ~5.8% on guided 2026 OCF less capex (working-capital timing)
b1 flags ELV as financial so GP/A and leverage factors are blank
ELV.confidence_in_thesis: medium: valuation gap is wide (implied 3.1% vs base 6.5%), but earnings recovery depends on Medicaid/ACA/MA cost trend and is unproven

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ELV, so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile; dossier view is based on the reverse DCF only.

ELV.scenario_basis: Start 2026E adjusted EPS $27.00 (guidance floor); EPS growth -4/0/0% (bear), +10/+8/+8% (base), +13/+12/+11% (bull) a year to 2029E; exit P/E 11x/13.5x/15x; dividend $6.88 a year. Reverse DCF: owner cash earnings $22.95/share, CoE 9.0%, terminal 3%, implied 10y growth 3.1% vs base 6.5%

DHR.thesis_one_line: Leading maker of tools and tests for drug making and diagnostics, now more indebted after buying Masimo; good business, priced for too much growth.
kill_criteria: Core sales growth excluding respiratory testing below 3.0% in two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 +4.5%, Q1'26 +3.0%).
Consolidated net debt (debt carrying $26,558m less cash $4,348m, Note 10 and balance sheet) / (TTM GAAP operating profit plus D&A) above 3.25x at any fiscal year-end (now ~2.9x).
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance cut below $8.35 (now "$8.45 to $8.60", acc. 0000313616-26-000163).
Biotechnology segment core sales growth below 2.0% for two consecutive quarters while bioprocessing orders growth falls below 5% (Q2'26: +2.5% and mid-teens).
A Masimo-related criminal charge, or cumulative Masimo litigation payments and accruals above $500m (Apple, DOJ, Kiani matters, 10-Q Note 12).
key_adverse_facts: FY26 core revenue growth guidance top-end cut from 3%-6% to 3.0%-4.0% in July 2026; Q2'26 core growth +3.0% (+4.5% ex-respiratory)
Masimo acquired 10 Jun 2026 for ~$9.8bn cash (goodwill $4,960m, intangibles $4,844m); debt $26,558m vs cash $4,348m, net debt/EBITDA ~2.9x (derived)
Masimo legacy matters: Apple patent litigation, DOJ civil investigative demand and supplemental grand jury subpoena (27 Feb 2026), Kiani litigation
CEO transition effective 1 Oct 2026 (Blair to Sawyer Montgomery); special option and RSU grants to Steven and Mitchell Rales approved 31 Jul 2026
Goodwill and intangibles are 74% of total assets; Mitchell Rales sold ~1.08m shares (~$234.6m) Oct-Nov 2025 and CEO Blair sold ~$12.7m on 2026-08-21
data_conflicts: Yahoo total debt $27.9bn (includes leases) vs $26,558m carrying debt in the 10-Q
b1 classifies DHR under Information Technology (SIC 3823)
FY25 XBRL diluted EPS $5.05 vs release $5.03 (continuing operations labelling)
DHR.confidence_in_thesis: medium: franchise quality high; the verdict turns on price (implied 9.3% vs base 7.0%), with Masimo integration and bioprocessing conversion the swing factors

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for DHR, so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile; triage also said not to advance, for price-versus-growth reasons that the reverse DCF now quantifies.

DHR.scenario_basis: Start 2026E adjusted EPS $8.525 (guidance mid-point $8.45-$8.60); growth 5/4/4% (bear), 9/8/8% (base), 12/12/11% (bull) a year to 2029E; exit P/E 20x/25x/28x; dividend $1.60 a year. Reverse DCF: FCF/share $7.35, CoE 8.5%, terminal 3%, implied 10y growth 9.3% vs base 7.0%

HWM.thesis_one_line: Makes critical metal parts inside jet engines and aircraft, growing fast on record backlogs; excellent business, but the price assumes far more growth than likely.
kill_criteria: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance cut below $5.00 (now "$5.23 $5.27 $5.31" low/baseline/high, acc. 0001104659-26-091610), or Q3'26 revenue below $2,565m (low end of "$2,565 $2,575 $2,585").
Adjusted EBITDA margin below 30.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 32.1%; Q3 guide "32.2%" baseline, acc. 0001104659-26-091610).
Consolidated net debt (debt carrying $4,501m less cash $563m) / TTM adjusted EBITDA above 2.0x after Q4'26 (now ~1.4x).
FY26 free cash flow guidance cut below $1.75bn (now "$1,850 $1,900 $1,950" in $m, acc. 0001104659-26-091610).
Engine Products third-party sales growth below 15% y/y for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26 +32%).
key_adverse_facts: Price $232.48 = 44.1x FY26 adjusted EPS guide baseline $5.27 and ~2.0% FCF yield; reverse DCF needs ~17.5% 10y FCF growth vs base 11% and bull 14%
RTX and GE Aerospace each ~11% of FY25 third-party sales; aerospace ~70% of revenue (cyclical and concentrated)
H1'26 working capital absorbed ~$360m (receivables -$196m, inventory -$165m); H1 FCF/net income 0.75x; capex to rise further in 2027
CAM acquisition ($1.8bn, closed 6 Apr 2026) lifted debt to $4,501m (net debt/adjusted EBITDA ~1.4x, derived); Q1'26 GAAP EPS inflated by a $93m credit
Grenfell Tower claims (indemnified by Arconic Corporation) with trial anticipated Oct 2028 to Jul 2029; CAO sold ~$22.7m of stock Feb-May 2026 at $251-$270
data_conflicts: b1 GP/A -0.67 is an artefact of cost-of-goods presentation (GAAP gross margin ~34%)
Yahoo total debt $4.66bn includes leases vs $4,501m carrying debt
HWM.confidence_in_thesis: high on business quality and guidance record, low on valuation: the verdict rests on price (implied 17.5% vs base 11%); next_earnings_date is a Yahoo estimate (Q3 2025 was reported 2025-10-30)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for HWM, so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile; triage also said not to advance (re-rated to 37.7x NTM), confirmed here by the reverse DCF.
